Computers in Nursing Practice

Computers in nursing — hardware, software, basic skills and use in patient care.

🎯 After this chapter you can

  • Identify computer hardware and software basics
  • Describe basic computer skills for nurses
  • Explain computer use in nursing documentation

In simple words

Computers are now part of everyday nursing — documentation, medication records, test results and communication. Nurses need basic computer skills to work safely and efficiently.

A computer has hardware (physical parts) and software (programs). Nurses use both to access and record patient information.

Basic computer parts

Part Function
Monitor Shows information on screen
Keyboard Enters text and commands
Mouse Moves the cursor and selects
CPU Processes information
Storage Saves files and data

Basic skills for nurses

  • Turn the computer on/off correctly.
  • Log in with your own username and password — never share passwords.
  • Open, save and close files.
  • Use the electronic health record to chart and view results.
  • Log out when finished — never leave a computer unlocked.

Computer use in nursing

  • Document nursing notes and vital signs.
  • View lab results and imaging reports.
  • Check medication administration records.
  • Access policies, procedures and drug references.
  • Communicate with the health team.

🔴 Password security

Never share your login password. Log out of the computer when you step away — patient information is confidential.

Where the nurse uses this

  • Documentation — chart nursing notes, vital signs and care given.
  • View results — check lab, imaging and medication orders.
  • Medication safety — scan and check medications against the electronic record.
  • Information access — look up policies, drug references and procedures.
  • Communication — send secure messages to the health team.

🔴 Most important for exams

  1. A computer has hardware (physical parts) and software (programs).
  2. Nurses use computers for documentation, viewing results and medication checks.
  3. Log in with your own username and password — never share passwords.
  4. Log out when finished; never leave a computer unlocked.
  5. Computers store confidential patient information — protect it.

⭐ Important for exams

  1. Basic skills: log in/out, open/save files, use the electronic health record.
  2. Monitor shows information; keyboard enters text; mouse selects.
  3. Electronic health records improve legibility and access to information.
  4. Report computer problems to IT support — do not try to fix them yourself.

📌 Memory trick

Computer security: “L-O” — Log in with your ID, Log out when done.

60-second revision

  • Computer = hardware + software.
  • Nurses use computers for documentation, results, medication checks.
  • Log in with own ID/password; never share.
  • Log out when done; protect patient confidentiality.
  • Report IT problems to support.

Test yourself

Which is a computer hardware part?

Answer: B. The monitor is hardware (a physical part). Word, Windows and email are software.

Nurses should log in with:

Answer: B. Each nurse logs in with their own username and password.

Nurses use computers in nursing to:

Answer: B. Nurses document notes, view lab results and check medications on computers.

When leaving a computer, the nurse should:

Answer: B. Log out to protect patient confidentiality.

Patient information on computers is:

Answer: B. Patient information is confidential and must be protected.
